segments.visual: The code panel types one question two ways: the DataFrame line, then the same question in SQL.

sentences.text: Here's one question, written two ways: as DataFrame code, and as SQL. Higher-risk patients, counted by clinic.

segments.visual: Their physical plans appear side by side, node by node; every node matches, and the pairs light together.

sentences.text: Which one runs faster? Neither. Spark turns both into the same plan, step for step.

segments.visual: Series wordmark, Spark, Visually; Part I, How Spark runs a job; the episode title.

sentences.text: Welcome to Spark, Visually.
Today: say what, not how.

segments.visual: The SQL's first plan on the driver desk: plain names, the table unresolved. Analysis looks each one up in the catalog, and each column gains its type.

sentences.text: First, Spark reads what you wrote and looks up every name: the table, and each column, with its type.
In classic PySpark, that happens line by line, as you write.

segments.visual: Line 5 types: df.filter(F.col("xx") == 1). It fails at once with an unresolved column; no job ran. A caption: over Spark Connect, the same error waits for the first action.

sentences.text: So a misspelt column fails right there, on its own line, before a single task runs.
Over Spark Connect, the same error waits until the first action.

segments.visual: The analysed plan on the desk: count per clinic, filter, read. The filter slides down into the read, and a new step appears beside it: isnotnull(x).

sentences.text: Then the optimiser rewrites the plan. It pushes the filter down into the read, and adds a check you never wrote: that x isn't null.

segments.visual: The read's column list: patient, clinic, x, y. Patient and y fade out; clinic and x stay.

sentences.text: It also drops every column nobody asked for. This query needs only clinic and x, so the read takes 2 of the 4.
sentences.say: It also drops every column nobody asked for. This query needs only clinic and x, so the read takes two of the four.

sentences.text: You said what you wanted. Spark chose the steps, and their order.

segments.visual: The cast scaled up ten thousand times, sorted by risk, written as one Parquet file of 25 row groups; each group shows the smallest and largest x it holds.

sentences.text: Here's why that pays. Take the cast ten thousand times over, sorted by risk, in one file of 25 row groups.
sentences.say: Here's why that pays. Take the cast ten thousand times over, sorted by risk, in one file of twenty-five row groups.

sentences.text: Each group records the smallest and largest x it holds.

segments.visual: With pushdown, the 13 groups whose largest x is 0 grey out, and 12 are read. Only clinic and x leave the shelf: about 2.6 kB, against 1.9 MB for every column of those groups. A settings card turns pushdown off, and all 25 groups are read.

sentences.text: With the filter pushed down, the reader skips the 13 groups that can't hold a higher-risk patient. Of the 12 it reads, it fetches just two columns: about 2.6 kilobytes, where all four would be nearly 2 megabytes.
sentences.say: With the filter pushed down, the reader skips the thirteen groups that can't hold a higher-risk patient. Of the twelve it reads, it fetches just two columns: about two point six kilobytes, where all four would be nearly two megabytes.

sentences.text: Those sizes belong to this sorted file. Unsorted, every group holds both kinds, and nothing is skipped.
Turn pushdown off, and every group is read.

segments.visual: The single count on the desk splits in two: a partial count before an Exchange, a final count after it, with Episode 4's wall between.

sentences.text: Last, Spark picks real operators. The one count becomes two: a partial count on each pile, an exchange, and a final count. That's Episode 4's wall.
sentences.say: Last, Spark picks real operators. The one count becomes two: a partial count on each pile, an exchange, and a final count. That's Episode four's wall.

segments.visual: Line 4 types: q1.explain("formatted"). Its nodes light from the bottom: Scan parquet with its pushed filters and read schema, Filter, Project, HashAggregate, Exchange, HashAggregate, AdaptiveSparkPlan.

sentences.text: Explain, formatted, shows it all, node by node. The scan lists the filters it took and the two columns it reads. Then the filter, the partial count, the exchange, and the final count.
Before a run, it's the starting plan: adaptive execution can still change it. That's episode 12.
sentences.say: Before a run, it's the starting plan: adaptive execution can still change it. That's episode twelve.

segments.visual: Lines 6 and 7 type: the same filter as a Python function. The read's pushed filters are now empty; a Python worker appears beside each bench, and every row goes out to it and back.

sentences.text: Now write the same filter as a Python function. To Spark, it's a black box.
It can't push the filter into the read, so every row is read, and every row travels to Python and back, just to be checked.

segments.visual: On the scaled file: all 25 row groups read, against 12.

sentences.text: On our sorted file, that's all 25 row groups instead of 12. Keep your logic where the optimiser can see it.
sentences.say: On our sorted file, that's all twenty-five row groups instead of twelve. Keep your logic where the optimiser can see it.

segments.visual: Three recap cards: one plan for DataFrame code and SQL; the optimiser reads only what it needs; a Python function hides its logic.

sentences.text: Let's gather it up.
Say what you want, in DataFrame code or in SQL: it's the same plan. Spark checks the names, rewrites the plan, reads only what it needs, and picks the operators.
A Python function hides its logic, and the optimiser can't help.

segments.visual: The plan on the desk, with a price tag beside it: blank. Next: Part II, Counting walls.

sentences.text: The plan is chosen. But is it cheap? Next time, Part Two begins: counting walls.

segments.visual: Series end card with the next episode title.

sentences.text: This has been Spark, Visually. Thanks for watching the cluster with us.
